message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑documented dominant traits is the **presence of a mane** in males. The gene that controls mane development is inherited in a dominant fashion—if a male lion inherits the allele for mane growth from either parent, it will typically express a full mane (though size and density can vary). This trait is a classic example of dominance in a wild mammal’s genome.
